translation_notes: The site the stratifier flagged (sites[0].line == 13, in the region's context) is `from classes import BASE, BF, EDM, ERC, MADSRDF, MIX, OAI, ORE, PREMIS, PREMIS2, PREMIS3, VRA`: BF/EDM/ERC/MADSRDF/MIX/OAI/ORE/PREMIS/PREMIS2/PREMIS3/VRA are johnjung/metadata_converters' own project vocabulary objects (verified against classes.py: plain `Namespace(...)` bindings, real IRIs, no external dependency) -- genuinely ns_import_project, rewritten `from classes_context import BASE, bf:, edm:, erc:, madsrdf:, mix:, oai:, ore:, premis:, premis2:, premis3:, vra:`. BASE stays a plain (non-prefixed) import: it is imported but never used as NS.attr anywhere in the region (nor anywhere reachable from it), consistent with declarations.md's `from myproject.vocab import something, brick:, unit: as u:` -- a mixed list is legal, only names actually used as namespaces become prefixes.

SAME split documented for the LexMalta/edmondchuc siblings of this stratum: RDF and DC (`from rdflib.namespace import RDF, DC, DCTERMS, XSD`) are rdflib's own namespaces, not project modules -- they cannot be given a __namespaces__ export, so RDF.type/DC.date/DC.title/XSD.dateTime became `@prefix rdf:`/`@prefix dc:`/`@prefix xsd:` + prefixed names instead of a prefix import (DCTERMS is imported but unused in this region, left as a plain import, same reasoning as BASE). classification minor-restructuring for the same reason as those siblings: two different namespace origins forced two different constructions in the same import block.

The one `self.graph.add((self.MEPA_CHO, p, o))` inside the for-loop -- add_isolated's own idiom even though this region's stratum is ns_import_project, and INSTRUCTIONS_403 §2 forbids leaving a bare .add() where an island covers the case -- became `+{ {self.MEPA_CHO} {p} {o} }(self.graph)`: the CALL-SUFFIX form (current-graph.md's `+{ ... }(store.graph)` example is this exact shape, an attribute holding the graph) rather than `@graph self.graph` + `+{ }`, since it needs no extra declaration line and works unmodified against an attribute access, matching the doc's own worked example almost verbatim. `now = Literal(datetime.datetime.utcnow(), datatype=XSD.dateTime)` -> `datatype=xsd:dateTime` is a plain prefixed-name substitution, counted under 'prefixed name' and not separately as 'typed literal' -- the value itself (datetime.datetime.utcnow()) is computed and non-string, so this is NOT a coercion_datatype site of the kind INSTRUCTIONS_403 warns about (Literal(...) with an explicit datatype= is kept verbatim, only the XSD.dateTime term is rewritten), and it is not `"..."^^xsd:...` syntax either, so 'typed literal' would misrepresent what changed here.

Restoring the binding (AGENT_BATCH's 163-regions case): the region is `@classmethod def build_mepa_collection_triples(self): ...` at module scope after extraction, dangling outside any class. Verified directly against the pinned commit that calling it as an ordinary classmethod cannot work at all in the real repository: MEPA_AGG/MEPA_CHO/MEPA_REM are set as INSTANCE attributes in MepaToEDM.__init__ (mepa_edm.py lines 34-38), but @classmethod binds `self` to the CLASS, not an instance -- self.MEPA_AGG would raise AttributeError on the class; and agg_graph/rem_graph, plain instance methods on DigitalCollectionToEDM (classes.py lines 196-213), would be looked up unbound through the class and called with one argument short. A second, independent bug in the same commit: MEPA_WBR is referenced bare (not self.MEPA_WBR) and is never assigned anywhere in mepa_edm.py -- NameError. Neither bug is introduced by this extraction or its translation. Followed the RDFLib/prez sibling precedent in this same corpus (a `demo()` harness, identical on both sides, appended after the region) rather than silently changing @classmethod to a plain method (which the extracted lines forbid touching): `demo()` builds a real MepaStub(DigitalCollectionToEDM) instance carrying the bindings the extraction lost, and calls the classmethod's own wrapped function directly via `.__func__`, bypassing the broken descriptor protocol without altering the region's own decorator or body.

`now`'s wall-clock value (`datetime.datetime.utcnow()`, stored as dcterms:modified by rem_graph) is neutralised by freezing `datetime.datetime` for the duration of the driver's run_pair call (unittest.mock.patch on the module-level class, reaching both exec'd sides via the shared sys.modules entry) -- not by editing the region, which computes it exactly as upstream does; see driver.py.
